the random and Kaufman initialization methods outperform Forgy and MacQueen initialization methods for the following reasons: (1) the random initialization method makes K-Means less dependent on the initial clustering and on the instance order, (2) the Kaufman initialization induces to K-Means a more desirable convergence speed than the rest of the three initialization methods.
the random and Kaufman initialization methods outperform other compared methods in terms of both clustering accuracy and convergence speed.
the random and Kaufman initialization methods are better than the rest of the initialization methods in terms of both efciency and convergence speed.

two main issues.
the empirical comparison of the performance of the K-Mean algorithm when using each one of the four initialization meth-ods.
the study of the impact of the initial clustering on the performance of the K-Mean algorithm and the impact of the instance order on the convergence speed of it.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the random and Kaufman initialization methods are the most suitable for the K-Mean clustering algorithm.
the Kaufman method is the best initialization method in terms of both efciency and robustness.
the Kaufman method is the best choice for initializing the K-Meens algorithm.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the random initialization method is the best choice for the K-Mean algorithm when the convergence speed is the most important issue, while the Kaufman initialization is the best choice when the quality of the nal clusters and the convergence speed are equally important.
the Kaufman method is the best initialization method for the K-Mean algorithm.
the Kaufman initial-ization method is the best method to be used with the K-Meens algorithm.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Kaufman method can be considered as an alternative to the random method in the initialization of the K-Mean clustering algorithm.
, in order to improve the efciency of K-Means, the initialization methods should be carefully selected.

, when using a clustering algorithm that depends upon initial clustering and instance or-der (e.g. the K-Meas algorithm), one should be aware of the initialization method used to initialize it, as it can affect the nal clustering and the convergence speed of that algorithm.
